title: Frequency of the symptom inner restlessness in psychiatric-psychotherapeutic treated patients
summary: Patients in psychiatric-psychotherapeutic treatment often describe inner restlessness. Inner restlessness is often experienced as painful and a burden on everyday life. Treatment with medication or psychotherapy is difficult. Up to now, there are no data available to describe inner restlessness, nor is it clear how many people suffer from inner restlessness at all. Based on our experience in another study (FeedRuhe; DRKS 00020814), we have developed a concept on inner restlessness. Now we would like to ask 300 patients of a psychiatric clinic whether they suffer from inner restlessness and how they experience inner restlessness. We also want to investigate whether men and women differ or whether people of different ages experience inner restlessness differently.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use

interventions.name: Psychiatric-psychotherapeutic patients are interviewed once about inner restlessness by questionnaire

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
undergoing treatment, ability to consent given, informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Incapacity to give consent, insufficient resilience to participate in a questionnaire study, acute suicidality, existing language barrier, diagnosed disorder according to ICD-10 F0 and F7
